headline: Chinese Experts Discover Met's 700-Year-Old Buddha Mural Was Hung Slightly Crooked
meta_description: A groundbreaking collaboration between Chinese conservators and the Metropolitan Museum reveals new secrets about a massive Medicine Buddha mural.
summary_short: Chinese conservators spent three years meticulously copying a 50-foot mural at the Met, uncovering that the Buddha's head had been misaligned by 2 centimeters.
body:
Zhang Jian, director of the Meticulous Painting Institute at China's National Academy of Arts, stood in the empty halls of Guangsheng Temple in central China and made a bold decision: he would bring the massive Medicine Buddha mural back to life. The 50-foot mural, which had hung in the temple for 700 years before being sold to raise money for repairs, now resides at the Metropolitan Museum of Art in New York. Over three years, Zhang led a team of artists and conservators to the Met, where they painstakingly recreated the entire work—capturing every crack, faded contour, and conservationist correction. The replica would eventually reveal something the Met's own curators had missed: the Buddha's head was mounted 2 centimeters off-kilter, a misalignment born from a fundamental misunderstanding of Chinese brushwork.

The project represents an unprecedented partnership between the Met and China's National Arts and Crafts Museum, formalized in 2024. The Met granted full authorization for prolonged study and shared ultra-high-resolution digital images—unprecedented access that required installing hydraulic lifts and specialized lighting equipment throughout the gallery. Zhang's team, including artist Han Maoyuan, sourced clay-rich mud and rice straw from near the temple itself, then spent months tweaking mineral pigments to match how medieval painters' materials would have aged over seven centuries.

This October, the Met will co-host an international symposium in Beijing about Chinese murals—the first time the New York museum has jointly held a major academic conference in China. The replica debuted at an exhibition in Beijing on September 24th, allowing this ancient work to speak to contemporary audiences across two continents, united by the patient hands determined to honor what time had weathered.
quick_facts: 50-foot Medicine Buddha mural painted 700 years ago during Yuan Dynasty
Chinese team spent three years recreating mural at the Met in New York
Discovery revealed Buddha's head misaligned by 2 centimeters in original display
Met-China partnership formalized in 2024, first joint academic conference in Beijing October
